title: Democratic Candidates Opposing Data Center Bans Secure More Midterm Wins
summary:
Democratic gubernatorial candidates who declined to endorse bans on data centers saw higher victory rates in the midterms than those who backed restrictions on AI infrastructure. According to an analysis of election results, 98% of Democratic candidates campaigning on pro-innovation platforms won their races, while AI and data center issues ranked only 19th overall in terms of what mattered most to voters.

The electoral outcomes stand in contrast to NBC News exit polling, which found that 56% of congressional voters considered data center concerns to be a crucial or major factor in their vote. Although voters who prioritized the issue broke heavily for candidates like Georgia's Stacy Bottoms 59-39 and Hinojosa in Texas 58-39, the overall results suggest that pledged bans on the facilities did not drive broader candidate success.
